text:
Dylan Strome finally scored on Saturday in Boston, snapping a 10-game goal drought (NHL.com's Tom Gulitti had the count), and it says something about his season that the drought is the headline. He has 18 points in 21 games, 14 of them assists, and his scoring rate of 3.0 points per 60 sits above our range for him. The assists have been fine. The goals are the problem.

That problem looks like luck. He has four goals on 6.5 expected, shooting 8.7% against a league norm of 13.5, and Washington has scored 5.5 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him on the ice. His minutes have slipped a little, under 16 in three of his last four games, while the Capitals lost six of their last seven.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had his shot assists in the 98th percentile last season. Evolving-Hockey noted the trade-off that comes with him: opponents got more chances with him on, bottom 4% of forwards. Watch the shooting percentage. It should climb, and the goal against Boston might be the first sign.
